result.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers
result.summary: The Key-Value (KV) cache is the main memory bottleneck of long-context LLM inference. Token eviction methods such as SnapKV, H2O, AdaKV and L2Norm shrink it, but they give every transformer layer the same budget, although layers differ in which tokens they need. We present MOSAIC, a multi-objective neural architecture search that learns per-layer KV-cache budgets for any eviction method. One search maps the trade-off between average budget and task score; its best allocation transfers to every target budget without further search, and an optional budget-constrained search refines it. Across four eviction methods on Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, MOSAIC beats uniform allocation in 146 of 154 (task, method, budget) settings, by up to +48 points on RULER and +11.9 on LongBench (LCC). On both models, it reaches the score of uniform allocation with up to 4x less KV cache (75% smaller). Against EvolKV, MOSAIC explores a ~10^40 x larger search space with 4x fewer evaluations and 18% fewer GPU-hours per budget, and scores higher in 5 of 6 settings. The learned allocations consistently favour a small set of middle layers.

AI.brief_summary: MOSAIC 用多目标神经架构搜索为每个 decoder 层学习不同的 KV-cache 预算，使任意 token 淘汰方法都能按层分配缓存；一次搜索给出的分配可迁移到不同目标预算，在 Llama-3 与 Mistral 上多数设置优于均匀分配，且学到的分配偏向中间若干层。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 LLM 推理效率工作，但按层分配信息预算、并发现中间层更关键的结论，可能为「缓存与层深如何影响 latent 状态及其可保留信息」提供可核查线索；论文未涉及多模态或 latent 推理，需自行判断迁移价值。
